chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) did not cease to advise me with the Siwak (brushing teeth) until I feared that I would lose my teeth or become toothless.'

key_terms.أَدْرَدَ: I would become toothless (lose all teeth)
key_terms.أُحْفِيَ: I would lose my teeth (become toothless)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet fear losing his teeth due to the Siwak?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the Sunnah of Siwak by linking it directly to the continuous revelation of the Angel Jibraeel, thereby elevating it from a mere hygiene practice to a spiritually significant act of following divine instruction. The Prophet’s humorous exaggeration about his teeth loosening (*ahfaya* or *adrad*) illustrates the frequency and emphasis placed on this ritual, which Shia scholars often cite as a recommended act (*mustahabb*) that purifies the mouth and pleases Allah. It serves as a foundational text for the cultural and religious importance of oral care in Islamic tradition, bridging physical cleanliness with spiritual devotion.
